title: G-PASTA: GPU-Accelerated Partitioning Algorithm for Static Timing Analysis
problem: Task dependency graph (TDG) scheduling has become the dominant bottleneck in parallel static timing analysis engines, preventing efficient exploitation of task-level parallelism on large designs. CPU-based TDG partitioning incurs prohibitive computational overhead that negates parallelism gains.
motivation: Reducing scheduling costs in parallel STA algorithms is essential for achieving meaningful performance improvements when analyzing large chip designs.
method: G-PASTA uses a GPU (graphics processor) to speed up partitioning—the task of dividing large task dependency graphs into chunks that can run in parallel. Normally, a CPU doing this partitioning is slow and becomes the main bottleneck in static timing analysis, preventing the parallel work from actually speeding things up. By moving partitioning to a GPU, which can perform many calculations simultaneously, G-PASTA makes this step so fast that the analysis can genuinely exploit parallel processing.
key_novelty: G-PASTA is the first to accelerate task dependency graph partitioning with GPU computing in static timing analysis.
contributions: GPU-accelerated TDG partitioning algorithm that drastically reduces scheduling overhead in parallel STA
41.8× speedup in partitioning runtime compared to state-of-the-art CPU-based partitioners
43% improvement in overall STA performance on large circuit designs
